fixes.explanation: Not quite, baker. Enemies running off isn't in this verse. God's reason is, "…the man who does these things will live by them." (Leviticus 18:5) The verse says nothing about enemies at all. The reason is about living.

Yep, and it's a blunt one, baker. God says, "Even the land has become defiled, so I am punishing it for its sin, and the land will vomit out its inhabitants." (Leviticus 18:25) I think this is a heavy picture. The land itself is part of this, and it is the land that does the vomiting out.

True, baker. God says, "…you must not commit any of these abominations—neither your native-born nor the foreigner who lives among you." (Leviticus 18:26) The native-born and the foreigner living among them are both named. Nobody gets a different rulebook.

Not quite, baker. God says the opposite: "So if you defile the land, it will vomit you out as it spewed out the nations before you." (Leviticus 18:28) Being brought into the land doesn't mean anything goes there. God spells out the "if," and the same thing that happened to the nations could happen to Israel.
